entries.name: ball lightning
entries.senseHere: A rare, still-unexplained glowing sphere that appears during thunderstorms, lasts a few seconds, and vanishes with or without leaving traces. The article treats it as a real but poorly documented atmospheric phenomenon, studied mainly through eyewitness testimony rather than instruments.

entries.name: Prairie Meteorite Network
entries.background: A US camera network that continuously photographed the night sky for over a decade to track meteors, whose archives were later searched for rare, incidental images of ball lightning.

entries.name: ALDIS
aliases: Austrian lightning detection and information system
entries.senseHere: Austria's network of ground sensors that detects and records the location, timing, and electrical strength of lightning strokes across the country, used in the article to cross-check ball lightning sightings against real lightning data.

entries.name: BLIDS
entries.senseHere: Germany's equivalent lightning-detection network, used in the article to confirm the timing and strength of a strike reported alongside a ball lightning sighting at Neuruppin.

entries.name: positive and negative lightning strokes
entries.senseHere: Lightning classified by the sign of electric charge it carries to the ground: most strikes are negative, but a notable minority are positive and typically far more powerful, a pattern the article found unusually common among ball lightning cases.

entries.name: spin quantization experiment
entries.background: A landmark 1922 physics experiment showing that the magnetic orientation of atoms is restricted to discrete values rather than varying continuously, a foundational result in quantum mechanics.

entries.name: Georg Wilhelm Richmann
entries.background: An 18th-century Baltic German physicist and member of the St Petersburg Academy of Sciences who died while experimenting with atmospheric electricity in 1753, his death later being wrongly popularized as a ball lightning killing rather than an ordinary lightning accident.

entries.name: keraunoparalysis
entries.senseHere: A short-lived paralysis or loss of feeling in a limb caused by a nearby lightning or ball lightning strike, distinct from longer-lasting psychological trauma from the same event.

entries.name: Jean-Martin Charcot
entries.background: A pioneering 19th-century French neurologist at Paris's Salpêtrière Hospital who taught Sigmund Freud and studied nervous disorders, including effects on patients who survived lightning-related encounters.

entries.name: triggered lightning
entries.senseHere: Lightning deliberately set off by launching a small rocket trailing a thin grounded wire into a thundercloud, letting researchers study strikes under controlled conditions rather than waiting for natural ones.

entries.name: soil strike theory
aliases: Abrahamson and Dinniss soil strike theory
entries.senseHere: An explanation proposing that ball lightning forms when a lightning strike vaporizes minerals in soil, creating a glowing ball of burning metal particles; the article cites a spectral analysis matching this theory's predicted elements.

entries.name: slitless spectroscopy
entries.senseHere: A photographic technique using a grating in front of a camera lens to split incoming light into its component colors without a narrow slit, letting researchers read the chemical makeup of a glowing object like ball lightning from its light alone.

entries.name: COST Action P18
entries.background: A European research-coordination initiative on the physics of lightning, organized under the EU's COST framework, which brought together around 30 researchers across Europe.
